passage_checks.locator_and_scope: Machielsen and Pfeffer, section II, paragraphs associated with notes 56–73. The named readers distinguish theoretical borrowing from ethnographic accumulation and retain Geertz’s objection; no direct reading of the original 1963 manifesto is claimed.
passage_checks.support: Uses anthropology to make historical belief intelligible while retaining an empirically particular form of inquiry.

passage_checks.locator_and_scope: Machielsen and Pfeffer (2023), opening and section III. Verified 2026-10-31.
passage_checks.support: Investigates past belief in magic and religion; his categories and account of decline have since been contested.

passage_checks.locator_and_scope: Existing source’s bounded primary Stone reading, pp. 3–6 and 13–24 only, and the preserved Keith Thomas roster context. Not Thomas’s assent to all of Stone’s narrative-revival diagnosis.
passage_checks.support: Provides Stone with an example of arranging historical stories around an argument.

passage_checks.locator_and_scope: Part 1, 51:15:24, explicit retrospective testimony. Bounded training influence, not automatic adoption of Hill’s Marxism.
passage_checks.support: Thomas identifies Hill as his main undergraduate intellectual influence and recalls the high scholarly expectations of his teaching.

passage_checks.locator_and_scope: Part 2, 43:02:10; part 1 school-reading recollection supplies additional context only. No claim of fresh Tawney reading.
passage_checks.support: Thomas identifies Tawney as a deep intellectual influence while distinguishing admiration from copying historical models.

passage_checks.locator_and_scope: Part 2, 36:50:21, explicitly distinguishes that attraction from hard quantitative Annales. Not allegiance to all Annales methods.
passage_checks.support: Thomas credits the Febvre strand of Annales with encouraging inquiry into historical values and mental assumptions.

passage_checks.locator_and_scope: Part 2, 16:43:03. Concrete publication encouragement and conceptual discussion, not the source of every anthropological idea.
passage_checks.support: Thomas credits Stone with encouraging the expansion of his Evans-Pritchard review into the history-and-anthropology intervention.
